findings.source_passage: could not find it in my heart to undervalue even a congregation of ants worshipping a toad-stool; or those other creatures in certain parts of our earth, who with a degree of footmanism quite unprecedented in other planets, bow down before the torso of a deceased landed proprietor
findings.why_it_matters: The extended satirical analogy about 'footmanism quite unprecedented in other planets' and the 'torso of a deceased landed proprietor' is Melville's voice at its most digressive and ironic; reducing it to 'ants worshipping a toad-stool' erases the social satire entirely.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore at least the 'footmanism quite unprecedented in other planets' clause; it is the rhetorical punch of the opening digression.

findings.source_passage: There was Queequeg, now, certainly entertaining the most absurd notions about Yojo and his Ramadan;—but what of that? Queequeg thought he knew what he was about, I suppose; he seemed to be content; and there let him rest.
findings.why_it_matters: This sentence pattern—the shrug, the charity, the 'there let him rest'—is one of the chapter's voice-establishing moments establishing Ishmael's ironic tolerance; it is wholly absent in the draft.
findings.suggested_fix: Reinsert the Queequeg/Yojo passage as a brief sentence retaining the 'there let him rest' cadence.

findings.source_passage: I wonder, thought I, if this can possibly be a part of his Ramadan; do they fast on their hams that way in his native island… It can't last for ever, thank God, and his Ramadan only comes once a year; and I don't believe it's very punctual then.
findings.source_locator: paragraph after I went down to supper begins
findings.why_it_matters: The wry aside—'I don't believe it's very punctual then'—is characteristic Ishmaelian dry comedy and interpretive of Ishmael's real attitude; its absence flattens the narrator's voice at a key moment.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the comic reflection on punctuality of the Ramadan; even a single sentence preserves the ironic register.

findings.source_passage: Think of it; sleeping all night in the same room with a wide awake pagan on his hams in this dreary, unaccountable Ramadan!
findings.source_locator: paragraph near end of night scene
findings.why_it_matters: The exclamatory, self-dramatising sentence is a register-defining moment; the draft replaces it with neutral paraphrase ('the thought of a wide-awake pagan on his hams in the dark made me wretched'), losing the rhetorical flourish.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the exclamatory sentence verbatim or near-verbatim; it is short and earns its place.

findings.source_passage: He looked at me with a sort of condescending concern and compassion, as though he thought it a great pity that such a sensible young man should be so hopelessly lost to evangelical pagan piety.
findings.why_it_matters: This is a critical interpretive passage—Queequeg's reversal of the missionary gaze is a thematic keystone the critical tradition highlights; the draft reduces it to 'he thought me pitiably lost to evangelical pagan piety,' losing the full ironic inversion.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the 'condescending concern and compassion' phrasing and the clause about 'such a sensible young man'; the ironic symmetry is the point.

findings.source_passage: barbecue all the slain in the yard or garden of the victor; and then, one by one, they were placed in great wooden trenchers, and garnished round like a pilau, with breadfruit and cocoanuts; and with some parsley in their mouths, were sent round with the victor's compliments to all his friends, just as though these presents were so many Christmas turkeys.
findings.why_it_matters: The grotesquely domestic 'parsley in their mouths… so many Christmas turkeys' image is darkly comic Melville at his most distinctive; 'I knew the rest' erases it completely.
findings.suggested_fix: Include at least the 'parsley in their mouths… Christmas turkeys' comparison; it earns the shudder.

summary: The draft preserves plot and several signature phrases but systematically flattens Ishmael's ironic, digressive voice across multiple passages—losing the social satire of the opening, the dry Ramadan-punctuality quip, the exclamatory night-scene sentence, and critically the Queequeg-as-missionary reversal—yielding four medium-severity findings that together trigger regeneration.
